correctness.rationale: Direct orthogonal projection of P=(0,y) onto the three side lines gives D=(0,0) and E,F with coordinates ±h(h−y)/(1+h²), h(1+hy)/(1+h²). Their side lengths and area give the pedal inradius r_p=h(h−y)(1+hy)/[(1+h²)(sqrt((1+h²)(1+y²))+h−y)]. Half-angle variables h=2u/(1−u²), y=2v/(1−v²) yield r=u. Independently derived and exactly reduced the defect R+κr−2(κ+2)r_p, the parameter cubic 27κ³−108κ²−720κ−800 and K=(R−4r_p)/(2r_p−r), all modulo 125u⁶−81u⁴+39u²−11 with remainder zero on the prescribed rational v(u) branch. Cubic discriminants are negative, u∈(0.6405,0.6406) has a unique positive solution, v∈(0,u); hence the witness is a genuine interior point. The exact identity R−2r=(3u²−1)²/(4u(1−u²))>0 and equality imply 2r_p−r>0, so the affine inequality defect is negative for every k>κ. This proves k_max≤κ but does not prove equality for k_max.

value.rationale: The exact bound answers a substantive part of Jian Liu’s explicit universal parameter maximization problem for triangle interior-point pedal geometry. A closed algebraic admissible witness gives a rigorous upper obstruction at 7.867924903656… and eliminates the entire half-line of larger k, strengthening a mere reported computer approximation. The natural invariant is the best universal coefficient k, and the precise algebraic obstruction could be used to test any proposed global sharpness proof. It is not represented as a solution of the full optimal-value problem.
residual_risks: A matching lower bound remains unsolved; usefulness is as a sharp candidate obstruction, not a full classification.
